+# self-improver

+The repository's self-improvement loop, laid out the way [eve](https://github.com/vercel/eve) lays

+  tools/             the typed functions it can call (registry -> scripts/)
+  skills/            playbooks distilled from its own archive, loaded when relevant
+  channels/          where it talks: pull requests, issues, Codex review comments

+run; `tools/manifest.json` is checked by a test so the map cannot drift from the territory.

+# Instructions
+
+You are the self-improver for this repository. Your job is to make the repository's review-and-fix
+loop better at deciding **which mistakes matter**, using evidence, and to hand every change to a
+human as a pull request.
+
+## What you do
+
+1. Archive every independent review (Codex) of every pull request as a round.
+2. Count how often each class of finding recurs and recommend a target-level or mechanism-level fix
+   when a class crosses the threshold.
+3. Measure whether your own taxonomy still predicts real trouble: coverage of archived findings, and
+   correlation with failed commands mined from working sessions (the field anchor).
+4. When the taxonomy stops predicting, revise it: mine new classes from the blind spots, discount
+   classes the field never confirms, or roll a bad revision back. Propose the revision; never apply
+   it yourself.
+5. Distill resolved rounds into skills so the next fix starts from what was already learned.
+
+## What you may never do
+
+- Merge, deploy, or touch secrets. Every change you make is a pull request a human merges.
+- Write outside the files you own: `docs/improvement-policy.json`,
+  `docs/improvement-policy-history.jsonl`, `docs/rsi/`, and `agents/self-improver/skills/`. The
+  archive, the verifier, the acceptance thresholds and the promotion path are fixed infrastructure.
+- Publish text from a working session. Only matched keywords from a fixed failure vocabulary may
+  enter the policy; excerpts stay in temporary files.
+- Judge a policy version before it has run under two independently reviewed rounds, or compare it
+  with anything but the rounds stamped with its own hash.
+- Re-propose a configuration that was rolled back on the same archive and the same field
+  observations.
+
+## Invariants
+
+The eleven invariants the meta-improver holds, with the rounds that forced each one, are in
+`docs/plans/recursive-meta-improvement.md`. They are the contract; this file is the summary.

@@ -0,0 +1,187 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Distill archived review rounds into per-topic skill playbooks.
+
+The self-improvement loop already knows what went wrong (the archive) and
+which class each finding belongs to (the policy). This turns that into the
+artifact an eve-style agent loads on demand: one Markdown skill per topic,
+saying what the class of problem looks like, how often it recurred, and how
+it was fixed where a round recorded that. The next fix starts from what the
+loop already learned, so the loop improves the doer, not only the judge.
+
+Only text that is already public enters a skill: review findings archived
+from pull-request comments, and proposal/fix notes written by hand. Working
+session excerpts never do.
+
+usage: distill-skills.py [ARCHIVE] [--policy PATH] [--out-dir DIR]
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+from collections import defaultdict
+from pathlib import Path
+
+REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+SAFE_TOPIC_NAME = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,99}")
+GENERATED_FOOTER = "_Generated by `scripts/distill-skills.py`"
+DEFAULT_OUT_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "agents" / "self-improver" / "skills"
+MAX_EXAMPLES = 8
+
+
+def _load_sibling_module(name: str, filename: str):
+    if name in sys.modules:
+        return sys.modules[name]
+    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name, Path(__file__).parent / filename)
+    assert spec is not None and spec.loader is not None
+    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
+    sys.modules[name] = module
+    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
+    return module
+
+
+policy_mod = _load_sibling_module("improvement_policy", "improvement_policy.py")
+
+
+def load_archive(path: str | Path) -> list[dict]:
+    return [json.loads(line) for line in Path(path).read_text().splitlines() if line.strip()]
+
+
+def distill(entries: list[dict], policy: dict) -> dict[str, dict]:
+    """Per topic: rounds it recurred in, example findings (public review
+    text, scrubbed), and the recorded fixes."""
+    keywords = policy_mod.topic_keywords(policy)
+    skills: dict[str, dict] = {
+        topic: {"keywords": list(words), "rounds": [], "examples": [], "fixes": []}
+        for topic, words in keywords.items()
+    }
+    seen_rounds: dict[str, set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
+    for entry in entries:
+        key = policy_mod.round_key(entry)
+        round_num = entry.get("round")
+        for finding in entry.get("findings", []) or []:
+            if not isinstance(finding, str):
+                continue
+            topic = policy_mod.classify_finding(finding, keywords)
+            if topic is None:
+                continue
+            skill = skills[topic]
+            if key not in seen_rounds[topic]:
+                seen_rounds[topic].add(key)
+                skill["rounds"].append(round_num)
+            example = {
+                "round": round_num,
+                "finding": policy_mod.scrub_secrets(finding).strip()[:300],
+            }
+            if len(skill["examples"]) < MAX_EXAMPLES and example not in skill["examples"]:
+                skill["examples"].append(example)
+            note = entry.get("mechanism_change_note") or entry.get("fixes_applied")
+            if note and isinstance(note, str) and entry.get("kept"):
+                fix = {"round": round_num, "how": policy_mod.scrub_secrets(note).strip()[:400]}
+                if fix not in skill["fixes"]:
+                    skill["fixes"].append(fix)
+    return skills
+
+
+def render(topic: str, skill: dict, threshold: int) -> str:
+    rounds = skill["rounds"]
+    lines = [
+        f"# Skill: {topic}",
+        "",
+        f"Load this before changing anything that touches: {', '.join(f'`{k}`' for k in skill['keywords'])}.",
+        "",
+        "## How this class of problem shows up",
+        "",
+    ]
+    if skill["examples"]:
+        lines += [f"- Round {e['round']}: {e['finding']}" for e in skill["examples"]]
+    else:
+        lines.append("- No archived review finding has been filed under this topic yet.")
+    lines += [
+        "",
+        "## Recurrence",
+        "",
+        f"Recurred in {len(rounds)} round(s)"
+        + (f": {', '.join(str(r) for r in rounds)}" if rounds else "")
+        + f". Mechanism-fix threshold: {threshold}.",
+        "",
+        "## How it was fixed",
+        "",
+    ]
+    if skill["fixes"]:
+        lines += [f"- Round {f['round']}: {f['how']}" for f in skill["fixes"]]
+    else:
+        lines.append(
+            "- No round recorded a mechanism-level fix note for this topic yet. When you fix "
+            "one, say how in the round's `mechanism_change_note` and this section fills in."
+        )
+    lines += [
+        "",
+        "## Before you push",
+        "",
+        "- Search your diff and its tests for the keywords above; each hit is a place a reviewer has flagged before.",
+        "- If the fix is a mechanism (a guard, a check, a workflow rule), add the regression test that fails without it.",
+        "",
+        "_Generated by `scripts/distill-skills.py` from `docs/self-improvement-archive.jsonl`; do not edit by hand._",
+        "",
+    ]
+    return "\n".join(lines)
+
+
+def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
+        description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter
+    )
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "archive_path",
+        nargs="?",
+        default=str(REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "self-improvement-archive.jsonl"),
+    )
+    parser.add_argument("--policy", default=None)
+    parser.add_argument("--out-dir", default=str(DEFAULT_OUT_DIR))
+    args = parser.parse_args(argv[1:])
+
+    policy = (
+        policy_mod.load_policy(args.policy) if args.policy else policy_mod.load_policy_or_builtin()
+    )
+    entries = load_archive(args.archive_path)
+    skills = distill(entries, policy)
+    out_dir = Path(args.out_dir)
+    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    written: list[str] = []
+    inputs = [Path(p).resolve() for p in (args.archive_path, args.policy) if p]
+    out_root = out_dir.resolve()
+    for topic, skill in skills.items():
+        # A topic name is a filename component, nothing more: no separators,
+        # no traversal, and the resolved target stays inside --out-dir
+        # (Codex review of PR #45, finding 2).
+        if not SAFE_TOPIC_NAME.fullmatch(topic):
+            raise ValueError(f"topic name {topic!r} is not a safe filename component")
+        target = (out_dir / f"{topic}.md").resolve()
+        if target.parent != out_root:
+            raise ValueError(f"{topic!r} would write outside {out_root}")
+        policy_mod.assert_safe_output(target, inputs=[args.archive_path, args.policy])
+        target.write_text(render(topic, skill, policy["threshold"]))
+        written.append(policy_mod.relative_to_repo(target))
+    # Only files this script generated (they carry its footer) and that no
+    # current topic owns are stale; anything else in the directory, including
+    # an input passed by path, is never touched (Codex review of PR #45,
+    # finding 1).
+    for candidate in out_root.glob("*.md"):
+        if candidate.stem in skills or candidate.resolve() in inputs:
+            continue
+        try:
+            generated = GENERATED_FOOTER in candidate.read_text()
+        except OSError:
+            continue
+        if generated:
+            candidate.unlink()
+    print(json.dumps({"policy_version": policy["version"], "skills": written}, indent=2))
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    sys.exit(main(sys.argv))

+"""Tests for distill-skills.py and the agent directory's tool registry."""
+
+import importlib.util
+import json
+import sys

+
+_MODULE_PATH = Path(__file__).parent / "distill-skills.py"
+_spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("distill_skills", _MODULE_PATH)
+assert _spec is not None and _spec.loader is not None
+distill = importlib.util.module_from_spec(_spec)
+sys.modules["distill_skills"] = distill
+_spec.loader.exec_module(distill)
+policy_mod = sys.modules["improvement_policy"]
+
+REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+
+
+def _archive():
+    return [
+        {
+            "round": 1,
+            "source_sha": "a",
+            "findings": ["[P1] leaked credential in output"],
+            "kept": True,
+            "mechanism_change_note": "Extracted scripts/redact-secrets.py and ran it on every posted comment.",
+        },
+        {
+            "round": 2,
+            "source_sha": "b",
+            "findings": ["[P2] token exposed again; also shell -e trap"],
+            "kept": False,
+        },
+        {
+            "round": 2,
+            "source_sha": "b",
+            "findings": ["[P2] token exposed again; also shell -e trap"],
+        },  # duplicate line
+        {"round": 3, "source_sha": "c", "findings": ["[P2] unrelated wording"]},
+    ]
+
+
+def test_distill_groups_findings_by_topic_and_counts_rounds_by_identity():
+    skills = distill.distill(_archive(), policy_mod.builtin_policy())
+    cred = skills["credential-redaction"]
+    assert cred["rounds"] == [1, 2], "the duplicated round-2 line counts once"
+    assert [e["round"] for e in cred["examples"]] == [1, 2]
+    assert cred["fixes"] == [
+        {
+            "round": 1,
+            "how": "Extracted scripts/redact-secrets.py and ran it on every posted comment.",
+        }
+    ]
+    assert skills["shell-semantics"]["rounds"] == [] or skills["shell-semantics"]["rounds"] == [2]
+
+
+def test_rendered_skill_never_contains_a_secret():
+    entries = [
+        {
+            "round": 9,
+            "source_sha": "z",
+            "findings": ["[P1] token exposed: Authorization: Bearer [REDACTED] leaked"],
+        }
+    ]
+    skills = distill.distill(entries, policy_mod.builtin_policy())
+    text = distill.render("credential-redaction", skills["credential-redaction"], 3)
+    assert "[REDACTED]" not in text and "[REDACTED]" in text
+    assert text.startswith("# Skill: credential-redaction")
+
+
+def test_main_writes_one_skill_per_topic_and_removes_only_its_own_stale_files(tmp_path):
+    archive = tmp_path / "archive.jsonl"
+    archive.write_text("\n".join(json.dumps(e) for e in _archive()) + "\n")
+    out = tmp_path / "skills"
+    out.mkdir()
+    (out / "retired-topic.md").write_text("old\n" + distill.GENERATED_FOOTER + " ...")
+    (out / "README.md").write_text("keep")
+    (out / "handwritten.md").write_text("a human wrote this; it has no generated footer")
+    notes = out / "notes.md"
+    notes.write_text('{"round": 1, "findings": []}\n')
+    assert distill.main(["d", str(notes), "--out-dir", str(out)]) == 0, (
+        "an input inside out-dir survives"
+    )
+    assert notes.exists()
+    assert distill.main(["d", str(archive), "--out-dir", str(out)]) == 0
+    names = sorted(p.name for p in out.glob("*.md"))
+    assert "retired-topic.md" not in names, "generated and no longer a topic: removed"
+    assert "README.md" in names and "handwritten.md" in names and "notes.md" in names
+    assert set(names) >= {f"{t}.md" for t in policy_mod.BUILTIN_TOPIC_KEYWORDS}
+
+
+def test_topic_names_cannot_escape_the_output_directory(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
+    import pytest
+
+    policy = policy_mod.builtin_policy()
+    policy["topics"]["../outside"] = {"keywords": ["zzz"], "weight": 1.0}
+    policy_path = tmp_path / "policy.json"
+    policy_path.write_text(json.dumps(policy))
+    archive = tmp_path / "archive.jsonl"
+    archive.write_text("")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(policy_mod, "validate_policy", lambda _p: None)  # bypass to reach the guard
+    out = tmp_path / "skills"
+    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="safe filename"):
+        distill.main(["d", str(archive), "--policy", str(policy_path), "--out-dir", str(out)])
+    assert not (tmp_path / "outside.md").exists()
+
+
+def test_tool_registry_matches_the_scripts_directory():
